completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh's missing task-lookup-lib.sh REQUIRED_LIBS entry and lint-json-channel-discipline.sh's check_emit_perline() variable-redirect false positive, both now green from source store and deployed copy with 0 real-corpus lint violations; added a permanent regression fixture case; audited 22 sibling fixtures and defensively closed two dormant instances of the same missing-lib gap (test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh, test-git-commit-scoped.sh).

memory_candidates.content: When a shell test fixture's resolve_candidate() (or equivalent) is deploy-tree-first, a source-store fix will NOT show up in a fixture re-run until a non-destructive redeploy (deploy-headless.sh, default mode, never --wipe) syncs the change into .claude/. Re-running the fixture immediately after editing the source store silently tests the stale deployed copy instead. Redeploy before re-testing whenever the suite under test resolves candidates deploy-first.

When a shared lib (e.g. task-lookup-lib.sh) becomes an unconditional dependency of a critical-path script (e.g. task-lock.sh), any test fixture that builds a minimal script tree via an EXPLICIT lib list (REQUIRED_LIBS/REQUIRED_SCRIPTS arrays), rather than a wholesale lib/*.sh copy, can silently omit the new dependency and either fail immediately or go dormant (stay green only because the exercised code path never trips the missing source). Audit by grepping test fixtures for the critical-path script's filename and checking each explicit-list fixture for the new dependency, not just the one known-red suite.

For a per-line exclusion-pipeline lint predicate (e.g. check_emit_perline()'s chain of `grep -v` stages), fix a new false-positive shape by appending one more targeted exclusion stage with an explanatory comment, rather than allowlisting the specific offending line or changing the flagged code. An allowlist is narrower than the defect class (any future instance of the same shape recurs); the general predicate fix is verified safe by re-running the pipeline's existing genuine-violation and negative-control fixture cases unchanged, plus a new regression case demonstrated to fail against the pre-fix predicate.
